title: Temperature-driven transition between momentum-resolved and disordered averaged Coulomb drag in 1D systems
authors: Mingyang Zheng, Rebika Makaju, Rasul Gazizulin, Alex Levchenko, Sadhvikas J. Addamane, Dominique Laroche
abstract: Advancing the understanding of electron-electron interactions in one-dimensional systems remains one of the central challenges in low-dimensional physics, especially for Coulomb-coupled Tomonaga-Luttinger liquids. Notably, the difficulty of reliably extracting one-dimensional system parameters, combined with the presence of disorder, has hindered the interpretation of 1D Coulomb drag experiments. Here, we present a self-consistent experimental determination of the relative Luttinger liquid interaction parameters through 1D Coulomb drag measurements, and achieve quantitative agreement with theoretical predictions. Utilizing vertically coupled GaAs-AlGaAs quantum wires, we fully characterize the one-dimensional parameters through magnetic depopulation. Coulomb drag exhibits a systematic evolution with magnetic field, reflecting the successive depopulation of 1D subbands and the suppression of disorder effects. Two distinct temperature regimes are identified, marking the boundary between momentum-resolved and disordered-averaged Coulomb drag. The observed scaling, peak broadening, and nonlinear current-voltage characteristics establish a unified and quantitative framework for probing electron-electron interactions in 1D systems.
summary: This paper reports on advanced experiments measuring Coulomb drag in 1D semiconductor quantum wires. By systematically varying temperature and magnetic field, the authors resolved a transition between two distinct physical regimes: one dominated by momentum conservation and another averaged over disorder. This establishes a quantitative method for characterizing electron-electron interactions in these complex low-dimensional systems.
main_problem: The study addresses the challenge of understanding electron-electron interactions in one-dimensional (1D) systems, particularly for Tomonaga-Luttinger liquids, complicated by disorder effects observed in Coulomb drag experiments.
main_result: The researchers successfully characterized 1D interaction parameters and identified two distinct temperature regimes—momentum-resolved and disordered-averaged—by analyzing the systematic evolution of the Coulomb drag signal with magnetic field and temperature.
method: Measurements involve performing Coulomb drag measurements (measuring induced voltage/resistance) in vertically coupled quantum wires while varying perpendicular magnetic fields and temperatures, complemented by magnetic depopulation analysis.
model_or_system: The physical platform is a system of vertically coupled GaAs-AlGaAs quantum wires acting as drive and drag conductors. The physics involves electron transport in quasi-1D Luttinger liquid regimes subjected to external magnetic fields and temperature variations.
key_observables: Coulomb drag voltage/resistance ($R_{Drag}$), magnetoconductance oscillations, and the crossover temperature ($T_1$) separating different scaling regimes.
important_parameters: Temperature (T), perpendicular Magnetic Field (B), Luttinger liquid interaction parameters (K), and disorder strength effects.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that the observed drag signal is dominated by momentum transfer when subbands align, and it models the transition between different scattering/relaxation regimes based on temperature scaling laws (power-law vs. Arrhenius).
figures_summary: Figures show 2D maps of $R_{Drag}$ dependence on gate voltage and B, demonstrating oscillatory behavior tracking magnetic depopulation; plots illustrate the systematic shift and suppression of drag peaks with increasing B, and fit results confirm power-law (Mid-T) and Arrhenius (High-T) temperature dependencies.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the experimental setup using quantum wires, details measurements across varying T and B fields to observe subband depopulation via magnetoconductance, analyzes $R_{Drag}$ oscillations tracking these depopulations, and finally maps out the temperature dependence to define the crossover between momentum-resolved and disorder-averaged drag regimes.
why_interesting: This work provides a highly quantitative experimental framework for probing fundamental many-body interactions (like those in TLLs) in low dimensions by using transport measurements sensitive to both quantum confinement effects (B-field oscillations) and thermal scattering mechanisms (T-dependence).
